model_source: NOAA NGOFS2 station nowcasts, nine 6-hour cycles
method: PORTS current speed/direction converted to u/v in m/s; observation times aligned to NGOFS2 station nowcast support by time interpolation with <=4-minute nearest-native-time guard. Surface, bottom, and depth-mean model representations scored separately. PORTS predefined-bin vertical equivalence to model sigma layers is not assumed.
interpretation: NGOFS2 captures some oscillatory principal-axis timing, particularly after aggregation and approximately one-hour phase adjustment, but absolute vector direction errors are large (roughly 75-95 degrees), sign agreement is near chance at many comparisons, and magnitude bias varies strongly by station and vertical representation. This materially lowers confidence in using raw NGOFS2 direction/magnitude as a precise Point Clear transport predictor. It remains provisional model guidance until local Point Clear observed-current validation exists.
guardrails: These stations are in upper Mobile Bay and do not directly validate Point Clear shoreline-normal transport.
Vertical equivalence is unresolved; poor bottom-layer comparison is not by itself proof of model bottom-current failure.
No production feature, weight, threshold, or forecast logic changed.
